# Ryan Vandersmith

> R&D software engineer building forecasting, visualization, and analysis tools for meteorology and atmospheric science.

Ryan Vandersmith is an R&D software engineer with over 10 years of experience and a deep self-taught background in meteorology. He builds weather forecasting and analysis tools used by photographers, storm chasers, and researchers, including Mesoview (skychaser.mesoview.app), a cloud inversion forecast tool, a mountain wave visualization tool, and a stepwise CAPE/CIN contribution to SounderPy. Professionally, he worked on Caffeine.ai, an AI website builder, and led Motoko programming-language tooling, including a VS Code extension with more than 85,000 installs. He also has experience with cross-chain EVM integrations, developer-experience products, UX research, Rust research software at the University of Colorado Boulder, consulting, and public-sector software.

## Expertise

weather forecasting and atmospheric analysis tools; MetPy, Siphon, Xarray, NumPy, and Pandas; geospatial and model data visualization; programming languages and developer tools; TypeScript, JavaScript, Rust, and Python; React and Node.js; WebAssembly; full-stack and progressive web applications; EVM integrations; UX research; data analysis; weather forecasting tools; technical mentorship.

## Career highlights

- DFINITY Foundation (July 2022 - April 2026): Led programming-language tooling and cross-chain integrations, contributed to an AI website builder, and led developer experience products.
- Plexa Technologies LLC (July 2017 - July 2022): Delivered full-stack Progressive Web Apps and custom web products for startups and small businesses.
- University of Colorado Boulder, College of Engineering & Applied Science (January 2018 - August 2018): Worked on Adapton, an incremental computing system, and built a Rust visualization tool for research on typed incremental computation.
- Halfbeard Web Design (November 2016 - November 2017): Built custom full-stack web applications with distinctive design styles for local businesses.
- Douglas County School District (June 2014 - August 2017): Built a bus tracking and route viewer, designed REST APIs, improved CI/CD workflows, and mentored the software intern team across four summers.
